Episodes.Description: When Peter's mother dies, he befriends her longtime pal Evelyn, who tries to seduce him. In the meantime, Stewie feels despair upon dealing with the realities of death.

Episodes.Title: 3 Acts of God
Episodes.Description: Peter grows frustrated when players on opposing teams continue to thank God after defeating his beloved New England Patriots football team, so he and the guys embark on a global quest to find God and ask Him to stop interfering with the outcome of professional football games.

Episodes.Title: Fresh Heir
Episodes.Description: Chris becomes the heir to Carter's fortune but refuses to accept the money; Peter desperately tries to keep the wealth in the family.

Episodes.Title: Secondhand Spoke
Episodes.Description: Peter takes up smoking cigarettes, and is approached by Mr. Stone, an advertising executive who wants Peter to be the face of his anti-smoking campaign under the caveat that Peter continues to smoke. Meanwhile, Stewie helps Chris battle bullies at school.

Episodes.Title: Herpe, the Love Sore
Episodes.Description: Brian gives Stewie an STD. Meanwhile, Peter and the guys fight back when another group claims their booth at The Drunken Clam.

Episodes.Title: The Most Interesting Man in the World
Episodes.Description: When Peter takes Stewie to the park for some quality father-son time, he mistakenly takes the wrong baby home, prompting Lois to call him an idiot. Determined to prove to her that he's a responsible adult, Peter goes on a business trip to Chicago and returns as an intelligent, classy person.

Episodes.Title: Baby Got Black
Episodes.Description: Chris is forbidden to see Jerome's daughter Pam, so when the kids run away together, Jerome and Peter must work together to find them.

Episodes.Title: Meg Stinks!
Episodes.Description: Meg has fun partying with Peter when he takes her to a college for an interview. Brian must learn how to live in the wild when he gets sprayed by a skunk and is prohibited from entering the house.

Episodes.Title: He's Bla-ack!
Episodes.Description: Cleveland returns to town, but is instantly banned from spending time with Peter when Lois and Donna get into a big fight over parenting.

Episodes.Title: Chap Stewie
Episodes.Description: When Peter and Chris interrupt Stewie’s TV time, the angry baby goes back in time to break up Peter and Lois so he’s never conceived, but is shocked when he is reborn into a “Downton Abbey”-esque British household.

Episodes.Title: The Simpsons Guy
Episodes.Description: In a special hour-long crossover with The Simpsons, the Griffins meet the Simpson family when they end up in Springfield after their car is stolen. Stewie takes lessons in pranks and skateboarding from Bart, while Lisa discovers - to her annoyance - that Meg is as good at playing the saxophone as she is. Peter bonds with Homer as they locate the missing car, but then they fight after Peter loses his job when Pawtucket Patriot is revealed to be a copy of Duff Beer.

Episodes.Title: The Book of Joe
Episodes.Description: Peter helps Joe fulfill his dream of getting a book published, only to take over as the writer. In the meantime, Brian develops an extreme thirst for exercise.

Episodes.Title: Baking Bad
Episodes.Description: Peter and Lois decide to open a cookie store, but Peter ruins things when he decides to bring clients in his own way.

Episodes.Title: Brian the Closer
Episodes.Description: Brian's cosmetic surgery leads him down a new career path as a real estate agent, which gets him into trouble with Quagmire.

Episodes.Title: Turkey Guys
Episodes.Description: On the night before Thanksgiving, Brian and Peter drunkenly devour the holiday bird, and then must go out to find a replacement. In Peter absence, Chris attempts to step up and become the man of the house.

Episodes.Title: The 2,000-Year-Old Virgin
Episodes.Description: After running into Jesus at the Quahog Mall, Peter is stunned to discover that the Son of God is still a virgin. So, he enlists Quagmire and Cleveland to help him throw Jesus the best birthday ever by finding a way to help him become a man.

Episodes.Title: Stewie, Chris & Brian's Excellent Adventure
Episodes.Description: To help Chris ace his ninth grade history class, Stewie and Brian employ the time travel machine for educational purposes. Not surprisingly, all three get stuck in the past.

Episodes.Title: Our Idiot Brian
Episodes.Description: When Brian takes the SATs for Meg but doesn't do very well, the family starts to doubt his intelligence; Peter tries to show Brian the upside of being stupid.

Episodes.Title: This Little Piggy
Episodes.Description: Meg is thrilled to be recruited as a model, but it turns out to be for a very specific type of modeling: the foot-fetish industry. Meanwhile, Brian accompanies Stewie on an open-road adventure when Stewie decides he wants to experience life outside of preschool.

Episodes.Title: Quagmire's Mom
Episodes.Description: After discovering his checks are actually a large size post-it pad, Peter demands he have access to the checking account. While at the bank, Peter & Lois discover that his first name is actually Justin, so Peter embraces his new partying “bro” lifestyle. Meanwhile, Joe arrests Glenn after he sleeps with an underage girl, which leads to an unexpected reunion.

Episodes.Title: Encyclopedia Griffin
Episodes.Description: Peter, Quagmire, Joe and Cleveland form a neighborhood detective agency, and are stunned to discover that Chris is a thief. Meanwhile, Lois is worried about Chris' delusional relationship with his new girlfriend, but also sees it as an opportunity for Peter to copy Chris' romantic gestures.

Episodes.Title: Stewie Is Enceinte
Episodes.Description: Brian decides he doesn't want to hang out with Stewie anymore, so Stewie tries to save their relationship by having a baby ... or seven ... by using Brian's DNA to impregnate himself. Meanwhile, Peter, Joe, Quagmire and Cleveland attempt to make a viral video.

Episodes.Title: Dr. C and the Women
Episodes.Description: Meg gets a new job at the airport, where she's instantly popular for being the hottest employee there. Meanwhile, Cleveland becomes a therapist and starts giving Peter and Lois relationship advice, but Peter quickly becomes frustrated and threatens to tell Donna a big secret about what went down at Cleveland's bachelor party.

Episodes.Title: #JOLO
Episodes.Description: When Peter accidentally discovers a missing child, he is hailed as town hero. Meanwhile, Joe quits his job and heads to Niagara Falls to live life to the fullest.

Episodes.Title: Once Bitten
Episodes.Description: After attending obedience school, Brian becomes much more submissive, and Peter realizes he misses his old, feistier pal. Meanwhile, Chris makes a new friend at school, but feels betrayed when he discovers it was all a ploy to get closer to Meg.

Episodes.Title: Roasted Guy
Episodes.Description: Peter's friends roast him. With his feelings hurt, he seeks refuge by befriending a group of gossipy women.

Episodes.Title: Fighting Irish
Episodes.Description: Peter claims he would beat Liam Neeson (guest voice Liam Neeson) in a fight, but when he is put to the test, he learns that winning is tougher than it seems. Meanwhile, Stewie becomes jealous when Lois decides to be a class mom and starts paying more attention to the other kids over him.

Episodes.Title: Take My Wife
Episodes.Description: Lois books a fun couple’s vacation in the Bahamas. But, much to Peter’s surprise, it turns out to be a marriage counseling program instead. Meanwhile, Carter watches the kids at home and becomes frustrated that they’re too into their electronics to play games the old-fashioned way. So he tries to fix it himself.

Episodes.Title: Pilling Them Softly
Episodes.Description: Stewie is diagnosed with ADD and prescribed Adderall, which Brian takes to write a 2000-page proposal to pitch to author George R.R. Martin at a book convention. Meanwhile, Quagmire and Peter compete, Iron Chef-style, to determine which of them gets to keep his new cooking show.

Episodes.Title: Papa Has a Rollin' Son
Episodes.Description: For Father’s Day, the guys track down Joe’s estranged father. But when Joe explains that his dad is intolerant of people with disabilities, Peter steps in and pretends to be Joe. Meanwhile, Stewie’s doctor tells him that he’ll only grow to be 5’1”, so he hangs out with Tiny Tom Cruise to understand what it’s like to be short.

Episodes.Title: Guy Robot
Episodes.Description: Stewie doesn’t like Brian’s stand-up comedy jokes, so the two of them fight. To get back at Brian and make him jealous, Stewie builds a robot friend. But when the robot outsmarts Stewie and dumps him, Brian and Stewie reunite. Meanwhile, Lois forces Peter to get a new mattress.

Episodes.Title: Peternormal Activity
Episodes.Description: The guys go to an abandoned asylum seeking inspiration for a new horror movie idea, but end up accidentally killing a man they think is keeping them hostage. Wracked with guilt, they each try to pin the murder on someone else. Meanwhile, Stewie is on a mission to destroy Brian's glasses because he's annoyed by how pretentious Brian's been acting when he wears them

Episodes.Title: Peter, Chris & Brian
Episodes.Description: Peter gets a check in the mail from the sale of his mother's home and he remembers that all of his old porn is still in there. When he returns to retrieve his stash, he finds a "to Peter from Peter" tape and realizes that his life has amounted to nothing. Reeling from his own failures, Peter then attempts to fix Chris before it's too late, and forces his son to spend time with Brian.

Episodes.Title: Peter's Sister
Episodes.Description: Peter’s sister, Karen, decides to come for Thanksgiving and bullies Peter the same way Meg treats him. While Meg is at first amused, she later feels badly and decides to help Peter train to defeat his sister in a wrestling match. Meanwhile, to avoid overeating on Thanksgiving, Stewie and Brian decide to go on a cleanse, which Stewie takes one step too far.

Episodes.Title: Hot Pocket-Dial
Episodes.Description: Quagmire admits that he is in love with Lois. Unfortunately, he proclaims his love while he has accidentally pocket-dialed Peter. Peter is furious and Brian takes it upon himself to fix the situation.

Episodes.Title: Brokeback Swanson
Episodes.Description: When Joe is trampled in a local running of the bulls and becomes a quadriplegic, the guys find it too difficult to hang around him. Meanwhile, Brian sleeps with a married woman, and when the husband returns home, he pretends to be the family’s new dog.

Episodes.Title: A Shot in the Dark
Episodes.Description: When Peter’s couch is stolen from his front lawn, the guys form a neighborhood watch group. While on duty, Peter sees someone trying to climb into Cleveland’s house and he shoots him. Peter is then arrested and charged with a hate crime. Meanwhile, Cleveland is touched when Peter finally admits to the accident, so he takes the fall for the crime and Peter is exonerated.

Episodes.Title: Candy, Quahog Marshmallow
Episodes.Description: Peter, Cleveland and Joe come across a VHS tape called “Winter/Summer” an Asian soap opera that Quagmire starred in when he was living in Korea. Unable to find the final episode of the series, the guys travel to Korea to find it and Quagmire is reunited with his old lover. Meanwhile, Stewie worries he might become a redhead.

Episodes.Title: The Peanut Butter Kid
Episodes.Description: When their bank accounts begin to run dry, the Griffins look for ways to make money. Stewie gets cast in a peanut butter commercial and becomes the money maker for the family. Meanwhile, Lois and Peter become crazy show business parents and Brian helps Stewie realize that he does not want to be a child actor.

Episodes.Title: Scammed Yankees
Episodes.Description: Lois and her mom, Babs, have a relaxing spa day, leaving Peter to entertain Lois’ father, Carter. The boys fall for an email scam, and have to go to Africa to get their money back. Meanwhile, Brian pursues Meg’s friend, Patty.

Episodes.Title: An App a Day
Episodes.Description: Peter overloads his phone with apps. He buys a new phone with more memory, gives his old phone to Chris, and hilarity ensues. Stewie joins a tennis club and invites Brian to be his tennis partner.

Episodes.Title: Underage Peter
Episodes.Description: Mayor West raises the drinking age to 50. Because of dog years, Brian is the only one old enough to buy alcohol, so Peter makes him buy all of his booze.

Episodes.Title: A Lot Going On Upstairs
Episodes.Description: When Stewie refuses to sleep in his own bed because of nightmares, Peter can’t stand it, so he goes to sleep in the attic. Peter turns the attic into a man cave and all of the guys begin hanging out there, which makes Lois incredibly angry. Meanwhile, Brian helps Stewie overcome his fears by building a device to go into his nightmares and defeat his demons.

Episodes.Title: The Heartbreak Dog
Episodes.Description: Meg begins working at a retirement community and starts stealing from the residents. Then Chris finds out and wants in on the heist. When the residents catch them, they blackmail them and force the thieves to listen to all of their boring stories.

Episodes.Title: Take a Letter
Episodes.Description: To pay for Stewie’s private school, Lois becomes a postal worker. She finds a letter from Peter that was never sent to his old fling, Gretchen, dated a week before their marriage. When Gretchen tries to come between Lois and Peter, Lois has a plan of her own.

Episodes.Title: The New Adventures of Old Tom
Episodes.Description: Peter gets lost in the mall overnight after his family abandons him. Meanwhile, Brian pretends to be a millionaire to win over a girl.

Episodes.Title: Run, Chris, Run
Episodes.Description: To everyone’s surprise, Chris wins homecoming king. However, Meg finds out that the cool kids plan to prank him during the homecoming ceremony, so they go to the school to investigate. Meanwhile, Cleveland starts hanging out with Jerome, the bartender. So Peter and the guys try to replace him.

Episodes.Title: Road to India
Episodes.Description: Brian falls in love with a tech support worker in India, so he and Stewie travel there to find her. Meanwhile, Joe invites Peter to his bingo night, but when Peter becomes the new center of attention, Lois helps Joe reclaim the group.

Episodes.Title: The Boys in the Band
Episodes.Description: Stewie and Brian form a band aimed at children, but face a breakup when they set their eyes on the same girl. Meanwhile, Chris gets a job as Quagmire's personal assistant for his sex life.

Episodes.Title: Bookie of the Year
Episodes.Description: Brian and Lois decide it's time for Chris to work out his anger management issues by taking up a sport. Chris surprises everyone and becomes a star baseball pitcher, which turns Peter into a gambling father, as he bets on his son's baseball games. Meanwhile, Stewie, Brian and Frank Sinatra Jr. attempt to open an Italian restaurant.

Episodes.Title: American Gigg-olo
Episodes.Description: After the local airline pilots go on strike, Quagmire looks for new work and becomes a gigolo. When his clients begin to avoid paying for his services, he asks Peter for help getting his money. Meanwhile, Brian is kicked off Peter’s health insurance, so he gets a job at a hardware store, until Stewie gets him fired and things get medical.

Episodes.Title: Inside Family Guy
Episodes.Description: Family Guy takes viewers behind the scenes of a regular production week, with James Woods as the guide. See the ins-and-outs of what goes into the making of an episode and watch the drama unfold as Peter is replaced and ends up in the office of Fox Television Group Chairmen and CEOs Dana Walden and Gary Newman to pitch his very own new series.

Episodes.Title: Chris Has Got a Date, Date, Date, Date, Date
Episodes.Description: Taylor Swift agrees to go to a homecoming dance with Chris after he asks her via online video. However, when she starts to fall for him, her music takes a hit. Meanwhile, Peter decides to try a new profession and sees firsthand what it's like to be an Uber driver.

Episodes.Title: Hot Shots
Episodes.Description: In order to "save" Stewie from autism, Peter and Lois decide not to vaccinate him and then proceed to convince the rest of Quahog to follow suit. Stewie runs away to save himself from diseases until Sean Penn swoops in to save the day and brings vaccines to the whole town.

Episodes.Title: High School English
Episodes.Description: In an anthology episode, the cast reenacts three classic pieces of literature commonly taught in high school: "The Great Gatsby," "The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn" and "Of Mice and Men".

Episodes.Title: Carter and Tricia
Episodes.Description: Carter buys the Pawtucket Patriot brewery and decides to cut some corners to save a few bucks. Peter overhears the plan and runs and tells investigative journalist Tricia Takanawa about Carter's plan to use toxic chemicals in the beer cans. Meanwhile, Brian's drivers' license has expired and he enlists Stewie as an instructor.

Episodes.Title: How the Griffin Stole Christmas
Episodes.Description: Peter fills in for Santa at the mall, but lets the power go to his head when he realises just what he can get away with. Meanwhile, Stewie and Brian become holiday office-party crashers.

Episodes.Title: Passenger Fatty-Seven
Episodes.Description: Quagmire lands free plane tickets for the guys' trip to San Francisco, but they begin to doubt his flying abilities after getting a look at the auto-pilot function. While in the air, sudden events give Quagmire's skills a run for the money.

Episodes.Title: Gronkowsbees
Episodes.Description: Rob Gronkowski moves into the house behind the Griffins. Stewie raises bees and sells honey at the farmers market.

Episodes.Title: Peter's Def Jam
Episodes.Description: The guys try to start a podcast, but Peter goes solo and branches out as a DJ. Meanwhile, back at the Griffin home, Lois' allergy forces Brian to move into Stewie's bedroom and the two have roommate difficulties.

Episodes.Title: The Finer Strings
Episodes.Description: The guys decide to form a string quartet, but Peter doesn't make the cut. Meanwhile, Brian is forced to be Carter's seeing eye dog and enjoys the life of luxury a little too much

Episodes.Title: The Dating Game
Episodes.Description: Quagmire discovers the “dating” app Tinder, forcing Peter, Joe and Cleveland to intervene and save him from his soul-sucking hedonism. Meanwhile, Stewie finds out that he has scoliosis and learns the perks of his latest diagnosis

Episodes.Title: Cop and a Half-Wit
Episodes.Description: Peter helps Joe out with several crime cases, but when Joe tries to take all the credit, Peter gets extremely angry. Meanwhile, Brian convinces Stewie to join a football team and panics when he gets a concussion.

Episodes.Title: Saturated Fat Guy
Episodes.Description: In an attempt to avoid eating the healthy food that Lois forces him to eat, Peter opens up his own food truck with fattening foods. Meanwhile, Meg joins a roller derby team, despite Chris thinking it’s too dangerous

Episodes.Title: Peter's Lost Youth
Episodes.Description: Peter gets jealous of Lois when she upstages him at a Red Sox fantasy baseball camp. Meanwhile, Stewie runs away from home when Meg is left to babysit him

Episodes.Title: The Peter Principal
Episodes.Description: Peter becomes the temporary principal at the high school, and Meg uses his new power to get even with her bullies. Meanwhile, Brian and Stewie open a bed & breakfast that quickly turns into a brothel.

Episodes.Title: Dearly Deported
Episodes.Description: When Chris' Mexican girlfriend, Isabella, gets deported, he volunteers to take care of her twin babies. After learning that Isabella can't come back to the U.S., the Griffins go to Mexico to return her children.

Episodes.Title: A House Full of Peters
Episodes.Description: Peter's past as a sperm donor catches up to him when many of his children show up unannounced to his house.

Episodes.Title: Emmy-Winning Episode
Episodes.Description: Tired of not winning an Emmy, Peter embarks on his own For Your Consideration campaign for Family Guy by making the show more like Emmy-winning shows - and no category is off limits.

Episodes.Title: Foxx in the Men House
Episodes.Description: Peter becomes friends with a cool, handsome paramedic named Stryker Foxx. Wrapped up in his newfound "coolness," he soon dumps Quagmire, Joe and Cleveland.

Episodes.Title: Nanny Goats
Episodes.Description: Peter and Louis find themselves with a golden opportunity to reconnect as a couple after Lois' parents get a nanny to take care of the children for them.

Episodes.Title: Follow the Money
Episodes.Description: Chris receives a special one-dollar bill as a birthday present, but he quickly loses it and the dollar passes into the possession of everybody in Quahog.

Episodes.Title: Three Directors
Episodes.Description: The story of Peter's firing from the brewery, as told in the styles of Quentin Tarantino, Wes Anderson, and Michael Bay.

Episodes.Title: The D in Apartment 23
Episodes.Description: When Brian posts an offensive tweet that goes viral and the rest of the Griffins are also treated as outcasts, he's forced to move out of the Griffin house.

Episodes.Title: Petey IV
Episodes.Description: Vladimir Putin comes to Quahog after Peter writes to him about an alternate ending to the Russian version of Rocky IV (1985).

Episodes.Title: Crimes and Meg's Demeanor
Episodes.Description: Peter encourages Meg to attend a high school party, where she takes up drinking, which both concerns and delights her father. Meanwhile, Brian begins spying on his neighbors and suspects Principal Shepherd of a crime.

Episodes.Title: Don't Be a Dickens at Christmas
Episodes.Description: In this special holiday episode, a selfish Peter loses his Christmas spirit and is visited by ghosts of Christmas past, present and future who take him on a journey around Quahog in the style of Charles Dickens' "A Christmas Carol".

Episodes.Title: Boy (Dog) Meets Girl (Dog)
Episodes.Description: Brian is smitten with a female show dog and enters a show dog competition in which the winner gets to breed her; Peter and Lois go to extreme measures to try to convince Chris that Arthur Valentine doesn't exist.

Episodes.Title: Dog Bites Bear
Episodes.Description: Stewie and Brian get into a friendship-ending fight after Brian commits a terrible act to one of Stewie's beloved toys. Meanwhile, Peter refuses to wash his hand after meeting his favorite breakfast cereal mascot, Boo Berry.

Episodes.Title: Send in Stewie, Please
Episodes.Description: When Stewie gets sent to see his school's child psychologist for a surprising session, he reveals major secrets about himself.

Episodes.Title: V Is for Mystery
Episodes.Description: Stewie and Brian are detectives who embark on solving a string of mysterious murders set in Victorian-era London.

Episodes.Title: Veteran Guy
Episodes.Description: After Peter and the guys get caught pretending to be military veterans and are found guilty of the Stolen Valor Act, a judge sentences them to join the U.S. Coast Guard.

Episodes.Title: The Woof of Wall Street
Episodes.Description: Brian convinces Stewie to teach him how to invest in the stock market after learning Stewie has a knack for making money from it. Meanwhile, Peter, Quagmire, Cleveland, and Joe look after the Drunken Clam while Jerome is away.

Episodes.Title: 'Family Guy' Through The Years
Episodes.Description: FAMILY GUY is reimagined as a series that’s been on the air for 60 years and, in a special retrospective, it looks back at the cultural events and issues that were tackled on the show in the 1950s, '60s and '70s.

Episodes.Title: Switch the Flip
Episodes.Description: To help get Brian's life in order, Stewie and Brian swap bodies using a machine that Stewie invents, but chaos quickly ensues around Quahog when the machine goes haywire.

Episodes.Title: HTTPete
Episodes.Description: To help promote the brewery to millennials, Peter adopts the millennial lifestyle, and his methods soon attract the attention of a high-powered Silicon Valley executive.

Episodes.Title: The Unkindest Cut
Episodes.Description: Quagmire's most treasured body part gets cut off in a freak accident and he is forced to learn how to live without it. Meanwhile, Stewie and Brian search for Mort after learning there is a $10,000 reward for turning him into the police for his involvement in a drug scam.

Episodes.Title: Are You There God? It's Me, Peter
Episodes.Description: After Peter falls into a coma, Peter meets God face-to-face, which leads him to ask some of life's tough questions.

Episodes.Title: Married... with Cancer (1)
Episodes.Description: Brian quickly falls in love with a woman, and after receiving devastating news regarding her cancer diagnosis, he proposes marriage.

Episodes.Title: Dead Dog Walking (2)
Episodes.Description: Brian's marriage to Jess doesn't go as planned, especially after her miraculous cancer recovery, so at Peter's suggestion, Brian lets himself go, leading Jess to make a surprising decision.

Episodes.Title: Pal Stewie
Episodes.Description: Stewie is surprised when he makes friends with another boy his age, but later taken aback when he learns that Stewie wasn't invited to his birthday party.

Episodes.Title: Big Trouble in Little Quahog
Episodes.Description: Stewie invents a shrinking machine that shrinks him and Brian down to microscopic size.

Episodes.Title: Regarding Carter
Episodes.Description: Lois receives a surprising birthday present from her father, Carter Pewterschmidt, that leads to an unfortunate accident leaving him dependent on Lois and the Griffin's care.

Episodes.Title: Stand By Meg
Episodes.Description: After Meg saves Stewie from a choking incident, Stewie makes it his personal mission to create a better life for Meg. Meanwhile, Chris is sent to a vocational school.

Episodes.Title: The Griffin Winter Games
Episodes.Description: To the surprise of all the Griffins, Meg makes the U.S. Olympic team as a biathlete and competes in the Winter Olympics.

Episodes.Title: Con Heiress
Episodes.Description: Stewie and Brian compete for the inheritance of a wealthy, older heiress. Meanwhile, Peter and Chris battle for Mr. Herbert's affection.

Episodes.Title: Pawtucket Pete
Episodes.Description: The Pawtucket Brewery hires new bosses, who decide to change the company's mascot. In an attempt to be crowned the new face of Pawtucket Ale, Peter and Brian go head-to-head.

Episodes.Title: Hefty Shades of Gray
Episodes.Description: After Peter's hair turns white from a ghost-hunting adventure in his house with the guys, his new look grabs the attention of local news anchor Tom Tucker. Under Tucker's guidance, he learns the ways of reporting fake news, and soon becomes a senior crime analyst on Quahog's Channel 5 News. Meanwhile, Brian and Stewie attempt to help Chris improve his dating game.

Episodes.Title: Trump Guy
Episodes.Description: Peter is given the position of the next White House Press Secretary and the Griffin family gets ready to make a move to Washington, D.C.

Episodes.Title: Bri, Robot
Episodes.Description: Brian worries about the legacy he's leaving behind, so Stewie makes a robot duplicate as a living biography.

Episodes.Title: Trans-Fat
Episodes.Description: Peter is mistakenly identified as transgender, which leads to an unexpected event and an important learning lesson.

Episodes.Title: Family Guy Lite
Episodes.Description: After a mishap at work, Peter decides to take his health more seriously and diet with the help of Quagmire, Joe, and Cleveland. When Lois takes a stab at writing a romantic fantasy novel, a curious Brian and Stewie investigate to find out who she might have a crush.

Episodes.Title: No Giggity, No Doubt
Episodes.Description: When the guys volunteer to chaperone the high school prom, Quagmire hits it off with Courtney only to discover that she is his daughter. To his and the gang's surprise, Quagmire makes a serious effort to embrace parenting Courtney, joining Peter and Meg on an ill-fated father-daughter camping trip.

Episodes.Title: You Can't Handle the Booth
Episodes.Description: The Griffins provide DVD commentary on a recent episode and reveal never-before-told drama between Peter and Lois.

Episodes.Title: Island Adventure
Episodes.Description: In search of Stewie's cherished big wheel tricycle, that Peter threw out, Stewie and Brian embark on an adventure to "Garbage Island," a giant floating mass of trash out in the sea. Meanwhile, Lois tries to help Quagmire elevate his dating game, as he courts a middle-aged woman.

Episodes.Title: Throw It Away
Episodes.Description: After Lois reads a new book on the joys of decluttering, she challenges the rest of the Griffins to throw anything out of the house that does not spark joy. While all starts out well, Lois soon takes the decluttering to a surprising extreme.

Episodes.Title: Girl, Internetted
Episodes.Description: When Meg suddenly becomes internet famous, she and an excited Peter work together to build her following and create content for her new image that revolves around unhealthy eating. Meanwhile, Brian and Stewie revel in a new ride while Brian's car gets repaired.

Episodes.Title: Adam West High
Episodes.Description: When Brian's proposition to rename Quahog's high school "Adam West High," to honor the late Mayor West, is successful, he feels encouraged to run for office as Quahog's new mayor. The race takes a turn when Quagmire campaigns against Brian for the open seat.

Episodes.Title: Yacht Rocky
Episodes.Description: When the brewery announces it will be firing one employee, Peter is nervous he will be the one let go; the family departs on a Yacht Rock cruise that doesn't go as expected.

Episodes.Title: Bri-Da
Episodes.Description: Peter and his friends are sick of forgetting the million-dollar business ideas they come up with while drinking, so they strap on Joe's police body cams to record their every move. Meanwhile, Quagmire is trying to come to terms with an unexpected family development.

Episodes.Title: Absolutely Babulous
Episodes.Description: When Stewie receives a participation medal in his school's toddler games, he begins to question everything he has ever won. Meanwhile, Peter causes a fight between Lois' parents and must repair the damage he caused.

Episodes.Title: Disney's The Reboot
Episodes.Description: The network decides that it's time to explore some unique ways to reboot the series. When three versions of the reboots are shown to a focus group, the feedback takes some surprising turns.

Episodes.Title: Cat Fight
Episodes.Description: When Quagmire opens a cat café in town, Brian decides to take a stand to get the café shut down. Meanwhile, when Meg and Chris get in trouble at school, Lois becomes nervous and decides they need to go to church camp in order to find their way.

Episodes.Title: Peter & Lois' Wedding
Episodes.Description: The Wi-Fi goes out in the Griffin house, leaving the family with nothing to do for the evening. In order to keep the family entertained, Peter and Lois decide to tell the kids the story of how they met and fell in love in the '90s.

Episodes.Title: Heart Burn
Episodes.Description: To celebrate Peter and Lois' wedding anniversary, the Griffins present their own versions of three well-known love stories.

Episodes.Title: Shanksgiving
Episodes.Description: Peter gets himself arrested to avoid Lois' special Thanksgiving dinner; A secret that Stewie's been keeping from everyone is revealed.

Episodes.Title: Christmas Is Coming
Episodes.Description: When Meg takes Stewie to the mall to meet Santa, she has a surprising response. Meanwhile, Stewie is entirely scarred from the same experience and Brian tries to help him process it.

Episodes.Title: Connie's Celica
Episodes.Description: When Lois gets a job as the music teacher at Chris and Meg's school, a mean student decides to make Lois the target of her antics.

Episodes.Title: Short Cuts
Episodes.Description: When Brian accidentally becomes a local hero, an old street pal, and now a successful millionaire dog, reaches out and tries to convince him to get neutered. Meanwhile, Lois gets a pixie cut against Peter's wishes, so Peter retaliates by trying to out-embarrass her.

Episodes.Title: Undergrounded
Episodes.Description: Peter secretly gets a credit card and overspends the family money, so Lois grounds him. To plan the perfect escape, he builds a tunnel leading directly to The Drunken Clam.

Episodes.Title: Rich Old Stewie
Episodes.Description: Stewie's future life could not be going any better, living as a wealthy, old Mr. Burns-type man, until his retirement is interrupted by Brian, who brings news that Peter is dying.

Episodes.Title: The Movement
Episodes.Description: When Peter starts coaching for Quahog's minor league baseball team, he gets constipated during the national anthem and must kneel, unintentionally becoming the face of racial justice.

Episodes.Title: Baby Stewie
Episodes.Description: Stewie builds a DNA-altering machine that will allow him to remain smart forever, but the invention has the adverse effect and he instead transforms into what he should have always been - an actual baby.

Episodes.Title: Start Me Up
Episodes.Description: Peter's non-stop sweating becomes a liability at his company, so his boss tells him to work from home. Meanwhile, after Stewie and Chris cause thousands of dollars in damage to an electronics store, the two create a fake Kickstarter campaign with Brian to pay back the money.

Episodes.Title: Coma Guy
Episodes.Description: With a newfound love for rocking out to Van Halen, Peter gets in a car accident and falls into a coma.

Episodes.Title: Better Off Meg
Episodes.Description: When Meg is erroneously reported to have died in a car crash, she goes along with the story to start a new life elsewhere. Meanwhile, the Griffins experience a life without Meg Griffin.

Episodes.Title: Holly Bibble
Episodes.Description: Cooped up in a hotel room due to a big storm, the Griffins pass the time by reimagining three stories from the Bible.

Episodes.Title: Movin’ In (Principal Shepherd’s Song)
Episodes.Description: Principal Shepherd moves in with the Griffins after he is fired for fat-shaming Chris at school. Meanwhile, Brian sues Stewie for writing a series of children's books which portray him as an idiot.

Episodes.Title: Stewie's First Word
Episodes.Description: Stewie finally says his first word, and it's a swear. When Lois is shunned by the other moms, she tries to figure out where Stewie could have possibly learned it.

Episodes.Title: The Talented Mr. Stewie
Episodes.Description: Stewie "breaks up with" Rupert after learning that he used to belong to Chris. Unable to get over his feelings of betrayal, Stewie decides to take action.

Episodes.Title: Boys & Squirrels
Episodes.Description: When Peter injures himself and a family of squirrels in a chainsaw accident, Chris and Stewie take in one of the injured rodents to nurse it back to health. Meanwhile, a chiropractor fixes Peter's injury by realigning his spine - and restoring him to his "true height" of 6'5".

Episodes.Title: CutawayLand
Episodes.Description: Peter and Lois accidentally set up a cutaway gag together, which somehow transports them into the cutaway itself.

Episodes.Title: La Famiglia Guy
Episodes.Description: When Joe asks Peter to be the godfather to his daughter, Peter commits to his mistaken interpretation of the role so much that he becomes a real gangster.

Episodes.Title: Meg's Wedding
Episodes.Description: Meg plans her wedding to an unexpected Quahog resident. Meanwhile, Peter finds a new vest and on one of many adventures fitting for his new attire, his arms are torn off and he is left with tiny hands that have yet to grow back.

Episodes.Title: Wild Wild West
Episodes.Description: Lois and Peter are divided by differing views on who the next Mayor of Quahog should be. Upset at Lois' first choice, Peter seeks out the late Mayor Adam West's cousin, Wild Wild West.

Episodes.Title: Pawtucket Pat
Episodes.Description: Brian's new job as a journalist leads him to uncover that Pawtucket Pat, Quahog's hero and brewery founder, took part in racist actions against Native Americans. The town becomes divided on whether or not to remove the statue that commemorates him.

Episodes.Title: The First No L
Episodes.Description: When the family fails to help Lois with the Christmas shopping, she walks out on the family and the Griffins must try to save Christmas on their own.

Episodes.Title: Fecal Matters
Episodes.Description: When Peter makes it through a bad flu season without getting sick, the hospital asks him to volunteer as a nurse, but he finds himself at a crossroads when his mortal enemy, The Giant Chicken, is admitted to the ER. Meanwhile, Brian receives his genetic test results and learns he is part cat, causing him to have an identity crisis.

Episodes.Title: Boy's Best Friend
Episodes.Description: Brian bonds with the son of his new girlfriend. Meanwhile, Peter, Quagmire and Cleveland take a joy ride in Joe's new classic corvette.

Episodes.Title: And Then There's Fraud
Episodes.Description: After attending a baseball game, Peter and Chris are inspired to start a memorabilia business. Meanwhile, Stewie tries to combat aging by getting plastic surgery, but ends up taking it too far.

Episodes.Title: PeTerminator
Episodes.Description: Stewie designs a "Terminator" Peter robot to destroy Lois for trying to feed him broccoli, but when things don't go according to plan, Stewie and Brian must go on a Terminator-esque mission to save Stewie's life.

Episodes.Title: The Marrying Kind
Episodes.Description: Stewie gets a mail order bride from Ukraine and experiences domestic life. Meanwhile, Peter and Chris become addicted to free hotel breakfast buffets.

Episodes.Title: Customer of the Week
Episodes.Description: After feeling unappreciated by her family, Lois taps into her villainous side and attempts to win "Best Customer" at her favorite coffee shop.

Episodes.Title: Who's Brian Now?
Episodes.Description: Brian has a microchip that reveals he had a family before the Griffins, when he then seeks out. After meeting the richer, smarter Hendersons, Brian struggles to enjoy his life with the Griffins as much as he once did.

Episodes.Title: Young Parent Trap
Episodes.Description: Lois and Peter are mistaken for "young parents" by another couple at Stewie's school and invited to live in a millennial apartment complex, leaving Meg and Chris home alone.

Episodes.Title: Meg Goes to College
Episodes.Description: Meg deals with a college admissions scandal, while Brian embarks on a fitness journey.

Episodes.Title: Family Cat
Episodes.Description: Brian tries to convince The Griffins that their new adopted cat, Pouncy, is evil.

Episodes.Title: Tales of Former Sports Glory
Episodes.Description: The guys regale each other with stories of youthful athletic accomplishments. Cleveland was a teenage baseball player from Cuba, Quagmire was a bad boy tennis superstar from New York and Peter was an underdog boxer from Philadelphia.

Episodes.Title: LASIK Instinct
Episodes.Description: With her vision waning, Lois elects to get LASIK surgery, but exploits her new disability for monetary gain. Meanwhile, Peter, Chris and Stewie must partake in all the activities with Doug that his father neglects.

Episodes.Title: Rock Hard
Episodes.Description: While at an old record store, Peter and the guys recount tales of three rock legends: Jim Morrison, Muddy Waters and Elton John.

Episodes.Title: Must Love Dogs
Episodes.Description: Quagmire meets an avid dog lover, and pretends Brian is his dog in an attempt to win her over. Meanwhile, Chris helps Stewie track down the culprit who stole his Halloween candy.

Episodes.Title: 80's Guy
Episodes.Description: Impelled by nostalgia, Peter recreates movie scenes from his favorite decade; Stewie and Doug compete to retrieve a Frisbee stuck at the top of the jungle gym.

Episodes.Title: Brief Encounter
Episodes.Description: When Peter and Quagmire accidentally switch underwear, they begin to mimic the other's behavior. Stewie and Doug agree to commit each other's murders.

Episodes.Title: Cootie & The Blowhard
Episodes.Description: Stewie takes drastic measures when he thinks he is diagnosed with terminal cooties. Peter becomes infatuated with Bonnie's cooking.

Episodes.Title: Peterschmidt Manor
Episodes.Description: Lois and her father attend the funeral of Lois' childhood nanny. Peter and the rest of the family turn Pewterschmidt mansion into a hotel.

Episodes.Title: The Birthday Bootlegger
Episodes.Description: A new boss quells Peter’s favorite part about work: office birthdays. Stewie is put in detention and comes out a ruffian.

Episodes.Title: The Fatman Always Rings Twice
Episodes.Description: In noir-style, Peter/Mac investigates the disappearance of Meg/Sister Megan.

Episodes.Title: Christmas Crime
Episodes.Description: After a Christmas tree lightning ceremony Brian crashes into Mayor West's nativity scene causing outrage.

Episodes.Title: Mister Act
Episodes.Description: An accident leaves Peter with a high-pitched voice, so Jesus coaches him into fending off the choir boys; Stewie is attracted to Lois' new masculine physique.

Episodes.Title: The Lois Quagmire
Episodes.Description: At odds with Peter, Lois takes Quagmire to her high school reunion; the rest of the family must cover up the death of a pizza delivery man.

Episodes.Title: Lawyer Guy
Episodes.Description: Peter hires the town's new lawyer, Brick Baker, to represent him in litigation against his new neighbor -- who turns out to be Brick; Brian and Stewie become lobstermen and save Rupert from the perils of the deep.

Episodes.Title: HBO-No
Episodes.Description: The Griffins tell their own versions of three HBO shows: "Game of Thrones," "Succession" and "Big Little Lies."

Episodes.Title: Hard Boiled Meg
Episodes.Description: Meg is invigorated by her new role as a getaway driver. Meanwhile, Quagmire can't rid himself of the hiccups and implores Peter to kill him.

Episodes.Title: Prescription Heroine
Episodes.Description: After Brian sustains an injury, Lois gets hooked on his painkillers. Meanwhile, Cleveland refurbishes Peter's ping pong table, which becomes the hot spot in the neighborhood.

Episodes.Title: All About Alana
Episodes.Description: When Lois' piano student, Alana, comes to work for the Griffins, Lois is initially glad for the help, until she realizes Alana's intentions are more sinister than she thought.

Episodes.Title: Girlfriend, Eh?
Episodes.Description: Peter and Chris take a road trip to Canada to prove the existence of Chris' girlfriend. Meanwhile, Lois and Meg compete for the attention of a handsome handyman.

Episodes.Title: First Blood
Episodes.Description: The guys' physical prowess is tested at Mayor West's dude ranch. Meanwhile, Stewie thinks he's gotten his first period.

Episodes.Title: The Jersey Bore
Episodes.Description: Peter attends a business conference in Atlantic City with Preston. Meanwhile, Stewie helps Chris prepare for his role in Adam West High's rendition of "Romeo and Juliet".

Episodes.Title: Oscars Guy
Episodes.Description: "Family Guy" retells three Oscar-winning stories: "Silence of the Lambs," "American Beauty" and "Forrest Gump".

Episodes.Title: Bend or Blockbuster
Episodes.Description: Resolved to enjoy a family movie night, the Griffins take a road trip to Bend, Oregon, to rent a VHS from the last Blockbuster in existence.

Episodes.Title: A Wife-Changing Experience
Episodes.Description: Joe accidentally sees Lois naked, leading to a reinvigoration of his sex life with Bonnie. Meanwhile, Stewie is gifted an electric SUV and quickly embodies the "Range Rover" lifestyle.

Episodes.Title: The Munchurian Candidate
Episodes.Description: Lois hypnotizes Peter into satisfying her sexual proclivities. Meanwhile, Stewie renovates his treehouse in an attempt to win over Brian and Chris.

Episodes.Title: Unzipped Code
Episodes.Description: Cleveland is fired as a mailman after an ignominious mishap, but flourishes in his new job at the brewery.

Episodes.Title: Happy Holo-ween
Episodes.Description: Peter makes a hologram of himself in order to get out of menial household duties.

Episodes.Title: The Stewaway
Episodes.Description: During a game of "hide and seek," Stewie takes refuge in Quagmire's suitcase, only to wind up in Paris. Meanwhile, Peter and Lois take a getaway to Vermont, where Lois is intent on breaking Bonnie's Instagram "like" record.

Episodes.Title: Get Stewie
Episodes.Description: Stewie finds himself in public disgrace after a popstar unleashes her fan base on him for a benign comment. Meanwhile, Peter gets lap band surgery and enjoys the merriment of excess skin.

Episodes.Title: Carny Knowledge
Episodes.Description: Peter and Chris finish last in a "Generation Gap" game at a carnival, forcing them to try to reconnect. Brian starts to date a carny, whom he can't break up with even after witnessing some of her crude habits.

Episodes.Title: The Candidate
Episodes.Description: Stewie and Doug compete for the honor of class “snack captain”.

Episodes.Title: Love Story Guy
Episodes.Description: The guys recount their first true love stories, leading to parodies of "Castaway," "Dirty Dancing" and various Meg Ryan rom-coms.

Episodes.Title: Old West
Episodes.Description: The guys try to help Mayor Wild West reconnect with his estranged father, Old West.

Episodes.Title: Single White Dad
Episodes.Description: Peter is mistaken for being a single parent, and relishes in the perks that come with it.

Episodes.Title: White Meg Can't Jump
Episodes.Description: Meg joins the Adam West High basketball team, and her play is fueled by Peter's lambasting from the crowd. Meanwhile, Stewie goes down a rabbit hole of conspiracies, which ultimately ends with him developing multiple personalities.

Episodes.Title: Adoptation
Episodes.Description: To restore his public image, Carter adopts a young girl from an orphanage, drawing jealousy from Lois.

Episodes.Title: The Bird Reich
Episodes.Description: To take advantage of a work policy granting leave in the event of a pet's death, Peter adopts the oldest bird he can find... and realizes it used to belong to Hitler. Meanwhile, after giving Stewie a signed copy of his book, Brian finds it in a free library, causing Brian to give up writing.

Episodes.Title: A Bottle Episode
Episodes.Description: Lois is blocked from a vacation rental app and accused of stealing after the family's trip to Nantucket. Meanwhile, Stewie and Brian buy saltwater taffy in bulk, and try their hands at door-to-door sales in the community.

Episodes.Title: Vat Man & Rob 'Em
Episodes.Description: When Peter gets a job as the new night watchman, he and the guys turn Pawtucket Brewery into an after-hours bar. Meanwhile, Stewie and Brian's plan to collect "lost dog" return money backfires when Brian is used for a dangerous TikTok stunt.

Episodes.Title: From Russia With Love
Episodes.Description: After Brian's Instagram is hacked, Meg takes Stewie and Brian to Russia, only to realize she'd rather stay there. Meanwhile, Lois reverts to her tormented teenage self when Quagmire starts dating her high school bully.

Episodes.Title: Adult Education
Episodes.Description: Meg gets married in Russia but returns home after discovering she was used for a green card marriage. Meanwhile, Chris, in need of an extracurricular activity, joins Principal Shepherd in shooting pornos at the high school.

Episodes.Title: Fertilized Megg
Episodes.Description: Meg agrees to be Bruce and Jeffery's surrogate causing a pregnant Meg to annoy her family. But, when the couple fails to pick up the baby, the Griffins must take care of their new family.

Episodes.Title: Supermarket Pete
Episodes.Description: With the brewery under construction, Lois implores Peter to take a new job, but grows irate when he begins work at the grocery store. Meanwhile, armed with his police stories, Joe and Brian team up to write their own true crime novel.

Episodes.Title: A Stache from the Past
Episodes.Description: When Peter loses the Griffins' home in a reverse mortgage, he and Mayor West travel to confront the man advertising the scheme, Tom Selleck. Meanwhile, Stewie and Brian open a booth at the flea market, leading to a rivalry with Bruce.

Episodes.Title: Old World Harm
Episodes.Description: Peter and Lois vacation in Florida, only to discover they've rented a condo in a retirement community. Back at home, Brian helps Stewie take his first shower.

Episodes.Title: Baby, It's Cold Inside
Episodes.Description: Peter is emasculated when, on their anniversary, he abandons Lois amidst a shark attack. Meanwhile, Stewie finds a mini fridge and lives the dorm lifestyle.

Episodes.Title: Boston Stewie
Episodes.Description: Stewie tries to civilize his half-brother, Boston Stewie, so that he may be adopted. Meanwhile, Meg and Chris start a venture in which people online pay Chris to sit on and smash cupcakes.

Episodes.Title: Snap(ple) Decision
Episodes.Description: Winner of a Snapple contest, Lois uses her winnings to take Meg on a tropical vacation. Flaunting their wealth, the two are kidnapped. Meanwhile, Stewie and Brian undergo "friendship therapy."

Episodes.Title: Baking Sad
Episodes.Description: Meg discovers her tears produce delicious cookies, and her, along with her siblings, enjoy a profit until the success makes her too happy to cry. Meanwhile, Peter and the guys launch a "male talk show."

Episodes.Title: The Return of the King (of Queens)
Episodes.Description: Lois decides to sell the family's television to help pay for Christmas presents, but when Kevin James gets upset over losing Peter as a viewer, he apparates into the Griffin house.

Episodes.Title: Cabin Pressure
Episodes.Description: When the Griffins win a trip to Maine at Peter's company picnic, they decide to invite their friends on the vacation. Tensions run high and things soon spiral out of control when the cabin burns down.

Episodes.Title: Teacher's Heavy Pet
Episodes.Description: Lois joins Chris's school as a substitute teacher, launching him into the cool kids club... but only time will tell how long he remains a member.

Episodes.Title: Take This Job and Love It
Episodes.Description: Peter and his friends wonder aloud about what their dream jobs would be.

Episodes.Title: Lifeguard Meg
Episodes.Description: Stewie and Brian become overwhelmed after winning a coffee shop. Peter and his friends annoy Meg at her new lifeguard job when they don't follow the pool rules.

Episodes.Title: Fat Actor
Episodes.Description: Peter tries to protest Hollywood after learning that Brad Pitt was cast in a biopic about a politician. After Pitt injures himself on set, Peter must act out the role himself.

Episodes.Title: Faith No More
Episodes.Description: Brian becomes romantically interested in someone and it inspires him to use Stewie's time machine. Strange consequences result from their journey.

Episodes.Title: Fat Gun
Episodes.Description: This "Top Gun" parody chronicles Peter/Maverick getting together with Lois/Charlie, the tragic death of Joe/Goose, and Peter/Maverick's blooming relationship with Chris/Rooster.

Episodes.Title: Live, Laugh, Love
Episodes.Description: When Peter realizes Joe has never found him funny, he is determined to make Joe laugh; Lois chaperones Chris and Meg's school trip, where she strives to reunite the principal with his long-lost love.

Episodes.Title: Drunk with Power
Episodes.Description: Peter swaps lives with Supreme Court Justice Brett Kavanaugh and is forced to make a ruling on the constitutionality of gay marriage, meanwhile, Brett tries to become friends with Quagmire, Cleveland and Joe.

Episodes.Title: Lois C.K.
Episodes.Description: Lois becomes a stand-up comic, using real life stories about Peter as content; Peter tries his best to straighten his life out to avoid being ridiculed by Lois's act.

Episodes.Title: The Chicken or the Meg
Episodes.Description: Meg starts dating a chicken she meets on a reality dating show.

Episodes.Title: Dog Is My Co-Pilot
Episodes.Description: After successfully landing a plane, Brian and Quagmire go on a press tour. Meanwhile Chris and Stewie open a boutique pizza place.

Episodes.Title: Pitch Imperfect
Episodes.Description: Peter must gain his family's respect back after he makes a humiliating throw. Brian and Stewie become chiropractors.

Episodes.Title: Hard Times at Adam West High
Episodes.Description: Chris uses Stewie's time machine to stop himself from having an erection during a book report. Peter becomes jealous when he sits out of a lottery pool and the guys win.

Episodes.Title: The Elle Word
Episodes.Description: When Quagmire starts dating a mystery woman, Peter, Joe and Cleveland go on a stakeout and discover her to be the librarian.

Episodes.Title: A Real Who's Hulu
Episodes.Description: The Griffins spoof "Only Murders in the Building," "The Dropout," and "The Bear."

Episodes.Title: China Doll
Episodes.Description: When Stewie sees a tag on Rupert reading "Made in China," he heads off to China to meet Rupert's family.

Episodes.Title: One Foot in Front of the Mother
Episodes.Description: Due to a police complaint about his excessive barking, Brian has to wear a shock collar; looking to join an after-school team, Chris discovers a talent for speed walking.

Episodes.Title: The Fat Lotus
Episodes.Description: In this Griffin-family twist on the popular HBO series, Peter suspects Lois of betraying his trust with Quagmire at a swanky vacation, while Stewie worries that his wealthy new friends plan to sacrifice him in a volcano.

Episodes.Title: Cool Hand Lois
Episodes.Description: Lois embarks on a journey of self-discovery.

Episodes.Title: Martian Meg
Episodes.Description: Fed up with feeling like she doesn't belong, Meg enlists in a training program for a mission to Mars.

Episodes.Title: Row v. Wade
Episodes.Description: Brian wins a boat on "The Price is Right" and decides to sail to Texas to help women seeking legal abortions.

Episodes.Title: Karenheit 451
Episodes.Description: Lois becomes the leader of a group of mothers who want to ban books from schools.

Episodes.Title: Twain's World
Episodes.Description: In an effort to improve his writing, Brian convinces Stewie to go back in time and bring Mark Twain to the present day, but the plan goes awry when Twain overindulges in pornography.

Entries.Title: The Simpsons
Entries.Description: Set in Springfield, the average American town, the show focuses on the antics and everyday adventures of the Simpson family; Homer, Marge, Bart, Lisa and Maggie, as well as a virtual cast of thousands. Since the beginning, the series has been a pop culture icon, attracting hundreds of celebrities to guest star. The show has also made name for itself in its fearless satirical take on politics, media and American life in general.

Episodes.Title: Simpsons Roasting on an Open Fire
Episodes.Description: Homer's Christmas bonus is canceled and the rainy-day funds are needed to pay for Bart's tattoo removal.

Episodes.Title: Bart the Genius
Episodes.Description: Bart's labeled a genius and sent to a school for the gifted.

Episodes.Title: Homer's Odyssey
Episodes.Description: After being fired from the nuclear power plant for negligence, Homer becomes a safety activist.

Episodes.Title: There's No Disgrace Like Home
Episodes.Description: After seeing families being nice to each other at a company picnic, Homer orders the Simpsons to a family therapist.

Episodes.Title: Bart the General
Episodes.Description: Terrorized by the school bully, Bart seeks counsel from Grandpa Simpson, who takes him to a warfare expert for basic training.

Episodes.Title: Moaning Lisa
Episodes.Description: The meaning of life and second grade have Lisa playing the blues solo--until she jams with a kindred spirit; Homer seeks tutelage to beat Bart at video boxing.

Episodes.Title: The Call of the Simpsons
Episodes.Description: The Simpsons put the wild back in the wilderness when their RV goes over a cliff and Homer and Bart go for help, get lost and lose their clothes.

Episodes.Title: The Telltale Head
Episodes.Description: Bart pulls a stunt that shocks the entire town, including the new friends he was trying to impress.

Episodes.Title: Life on the Fast Lane
Episodes.Description: Homer's bowling-ball gift "for Marge" prompts her to take up the sport--and maybe also a handsome instructor who offers to teach her "many things."

Episodes.Title: Homer's Night Out
Episodes.Description: Shutterbug Bart captures Homer with a sexy entertainer at a bachelor party.

Episodes.Title: The Crepes of Wrath
Episodes.Description: A little story about how Bart saves France after blowing up Principal Skinner's mom with a cherry bomb.

Episodes.Title: Krusty Gets Busted
Episodes.Description: Bart's TV hero Krusty the Clown is arrested for a convenience-store robbery, and witness Homer must testify against the clown.

Episodes.Title: Some Enchanted Evening
Episodes.Description: Homer takes Marge out for a romantic night, leaving the kids with a sitter--who's profiled on "America's Most Armed and Dangerous."

Episodes.Title: Bart Gets an 'F'
Episodes.Description: Bart fails four consecutive history exams and the school psychiatrist recommends that Bart repeat the fourth grade.

Episodes.Title: Simpson and Delilah
Episodes.Description: Homer uses his medical insurance to buy Dimoxinil, a miracle hair-growth formula. After growing luxurious locks, he's given a promotion which allows him to hire a secretary named Karl and makes grand promises to his family at home.

Episodes.Title: Treehouse of Horror
Episodes.Description: The Simpson kids hide in the family treehouse and tell each other spooky stories. The first regards haunted houses, the second introduces Kang and Kodos for the first time in an alien abduction, and the third is a Simpson-adapted retelling of The Raven.

Episodes.Title: Two Cars in Every Garage and Three Eyes on Every Fish
Episodes.Description: Bart catches a three-eyed fish in a river downstream of the Nuclear Power Plant. This causes the plant to become inspected, and in order to prevent it from being shut down, Mr. Burns decides to run for governor. After a hard campaign which sees Burns rise from being universally despised to running neck and neck with popular incumbent Mary Bailey, it is decided that Burns will have dinner with a random employee the night before the election. Homer is chosen, much to Marge's chagrin.

Episodes.Title: Dancin' Homer
Episodes.Description: Homer fires up the crowd at a Springfield Isotopes baseball game and is chosen to be the team's new mascot. He immediately becomes a popular attraction and the Isotopes start a winning streak. As a result, Homer is promoted to a team in Capital City, the Capital City Capitals.

Episodes.Title: Dead Putting Society
Episodes.Description: Bart and Todd Flanders decide to enter a miniature golf tournament. Homer becomes confident that Bart will win and makes a bet with Ned that the father of the boy that does not win will have to mow their neighbors lawn in their wife's Sunday dress.

Episodes.Title: Bart vs. Thanksgiving
Episodes.Description: Lisa makes a table centerpiece for the Thanksgiving dinner, which Bart accidentally destroys. After he is sent to his room by his parents, Bart angrily runs away from home and experiences a very different kind of Thanksgiving holiday.

Episodes.Title: Bart the Daredevil
Episodes.Description: The Simpsons go to a Monster truck rally that features famous daredevil Lance Murdock. Bart immediately becomes enamored and decides that he wants to become a daredevil as well. His first stunt ends in injury, but to gain the respect of his friends, he promises a far more impressive feat to them: to jump the Springfield Gorge.

Episodes.Title: Itchy & Scratchy & Marge
Episodes.Description: Maggie attacks Homer with a mallet after seeing it on Itchy & Scratchy. Marge begins a protest outside the production offices, demanding the show be retooled to prevent further violence.

Episodes.Title: Bart Gets Hit by a Car
Episodes.Description: After Mr. Burns hits Bart with his car, ambulance-chasing attorney Lionel Hutz persuades Homer and Marge to sue for a million dollars.

Episodes.Title: One Fish, Two Fish, Blowfish, Blue Fish
Episodes.Description: After eating poisonous blowfish at a sushi restaurant, Homer decides to live life to the fullest in the 24 hours he has left to live.

Episodes.Title: The Way We Was
Episodes.Description: When the TV breaks, Marge and Homer entertain the kids with the story of how they first met.

Episodes.Title: Homer vs. Lisa and the 8th Commandment
Episodes.Description: Homer becomes the most popular guy in town when he gets an illegal cable hook-up, but Lisa fears he will go to hell for violating the Eighth Commandment.

Episodes.Title: Principal Charming
Episodes.Description: When Marge begs Homer to find Selma a husband, he sets her up with Principal Skinner... who falls in love with Patty instead.

Episodes.Title: Oh Brother, Where Art Thou?
Episodes.Description: Homer's long-lost half-brother is the CEO of a car company that's wildly successful... until he hires Homer to help design a car for the average man.

Episodes.Title: Bart's Dog Gets an 'F'
Episodes.Description: After a series of destructive acts, Homer decides that Santa's Little Helper must go unless he passes obedience school. As the dog's last hours with the family approach, Bart must find a way to get through to him.

Episodes.Title: Old Money
Episodes.Description: When Grandpa's new girlfriend at the Springfield Retirement Castle dies, he inherits her savings and must decide the best way to spend his windfall.

Episodes.Title: Brush with Greatness
Episodes.Description: Marge rediscovers her interest in art and takes up painting. When Mr. Burns hires her to paint his official portrait, Marge tries but fails to find his "inner beauty."

Episodes.Title: Lisa's Substitute
Episodes.Description: With Miss Hoover out sick, a substitute teacher takes the class and becomes an inspiring role model for Lisa.

Episodes.Title: The War of the Simpsons
Episodes.Description: At a lakeside retreat for married couples, Marge is determined to fix her marriage with Homer, but Homer is more determined to catch General Sherman, the freakishly large catfish that lives in the lake.

Episodes.Title: Three Men and a Comic Book
Episodes.Description: Bart, Milhouse, and Martin pool their money to buy the new first issue of Radioactive Man, but their investment and their friendship are threatened when they can't agree on who will keep it.

Episodes.Title: Blood Feud
Episodes.Description: When Mr. Burns is saved by a transfusion of Bart's blood, Homer expects a handsome reward but is outraged to receive only a simple thank-you note.

Episodes.Title: Stark Raving Dad
Episodes.Description: A deviation from his norm lands Homer in a mental institution, where he shares a room with a man who thinks he's Michael Jackson.

Episodes.Title: Mr. Lisa Goes to Washington
Episodes.Description: Lisa's essay wins the Simpsons a trip to Washington, D.C., where her faith in democracy is shaken by her unethical Congressman.

Episodes.Title: When Flanders Failed
Episodes.Description: Flanders suffers a failure after Homer wishes him ill.

Episodes.Title: Bart the Murderer
Episodes.Description: While working for Fat Tony, Bart gains enough influence with his boss to solve his problems with Principal Skinner--perhaps permanently.

Episodes.Title: Homer Defined
Episodes.Description: Homer's averting of a nuclear meltdown earns him employee-of-the-month honors--and a call from Magic Johnson; Milhouse's parents prohibit him from playing with Bart.

Episodes.Title: Like Father, Like Clown
Episodes.Description: Bart and Lisa use theological arguments to try to reunite Krusty the Clown and his rabbi father, who disowned Krusty when he turned from rabbi to clown.

Episodes.Title: Treehouse of Horror II
Episodes.Description: Maggie uses one of three wishes; a mind-reading Bart rules Springfield; Homer donates his brain to Mr. Burns' science project.

Episodes.Title: Lisa's Pony
Episodes.Description: After disappointing Lisa, Homer buys her a pony, solving one problem, but creating others, requiring a second job--at Apu's Kwik-E-Mart.

Episodes.Title: Saturdays of Thunder
Episodes.Description: When Homer helps Bart build a soapbox racer, it does little for the car but a lot for their relationship.

Episodes.Title: Flaming Moe's
Episodes.Description: Moe steals the drink recipe Homer invented, and the rechristened “Flaming Moe” turns his tavern into a hotspot. When a national franchise wants to buy the recipe, Homer wants revenge.

Episodes.Title: Burns Verkaufen der Kraftwerk
Episodes.Description: Burns sells the power plant to a German corporation that doesn't care for Homer's approach to his work.

Episodes.Title: I Married Marge
Episodes.Description: A trip down memory lane to the early days of Simpson wedded bliss, when Marge was with child and Homer was without a job.

Episodes.Title: Radio Bart
Episodes.Description: Bart fools the town into thinking there's a little boy trapped in a well.

Episodes.Title: Lisa the Greek
Episodes.Description: Lisa's ability to pick winning football teams kicks off a strong bond with Homer.

Episodes.Title: Homer Alone
Episodes.Description: A stressed Marge vacations alone, leaving Bart and Lisa with Patty and Selma, and Maggie with Homer--until she leaves in search of Marge.

Episodes.Title: Bart the Lover
Episodes.Description: Bart's answer to detention from Mrs. Krabappel is to answer her personal ad with letters from a Mr. Wonderful, but his last laugh is more of a guilty whimper.

Episodes.Title: Homer at the Bat
Episodes.Description: Burns hires Major League ringers for the plant softball championship.

Episodes.Title: Separate Vocations
Episodes.Description: The results from their aptitude tests cause Bart and Lisa to make 180-degree turns in their behavior.

Episodes.Title: Dog of Death
Episodes.Description: Santa's Little Helper notices resentment after the Simpsons make sacrifices to fund his life-saving operation.

Episodes.Title: Colonel Homer
Episodes.Description: Marge fears a cheatin' heart when a waitress-country singer asks Homer to be her manager.

Episodes.Title: Black Widower
Episodes.Description: Bart suspects something rotten when Selma gets engaged to Sideshow Bob.

Episodes.Title: The Otto Show
Episodes.Description: Spinal Tap hits Springfield, and Otto the bus driver hits the skids after being fired, taking refuge in the Simpsons' garage.

Episodes.Title: Bart's Friend Falls in Love
Episodes.Description: Bart resents Milhouse's new girlfriend; Homer gets the wrong subliminal tape, which has him gaining vocabulary, not losing weight.

Episodes.Title: Brother, Can You Spare Two Dimes?
Episodes.Description: Homer's half-brother asks for a loan after Homer is awarded some cash.

Episodes.Title: Kamp Krusty
Episodes.Description: Bart leads an uprising at Krusty's summer camp after he and Lisa are subjected to a Dickensian sweatshop.

Episodes.Title: A Streetcar Named Marge
Episodes.Description: Marge is cast in a version of "A Streetcar Named Desire," playing Blanche to Ned Flanders' Stanley.

Episodes.Title: Homer the Heretic
Episodes.Description: After skipping church one Sunday morning, Homer decides to quit church altogether and spend Sundays worshiping in his own way -- with cigars and beer.

Episodes.Title: Lisa the Beauty Queen
Episodes.Description: Homer enters Lisa into the Little Miss Springfield Pageant to help her feel better about her looks. But when she must choose between the title and her integrity, she realizes that confidence comes from within.

Episodes.Title: Treehouse of Horror III
Episodes.Description: A Halloween trilogy includes a murderous Krusty doll; a "King Kong" parody; an invasion of zombies unleashed by Bart's incantation.

Episodes.Title: Itchy & Scratchy: The Movie
Episodes.Description: Bart is punished by being barred from the Itchy and Scratchy movie.

Episodes.Title: Marge Gets a Job
Episodes.Description: Mr. Burns is instantly smitten when Marge takes a job at the nuclear power plant.

Episodes.Title: New Kid on the Block
Episodes.Description: Bart has a crush on his new neighbor, a teenage girl who only has eyes for Jimbo Jones. Bart sets out to prove that Jimbo is not as tough as he seems.

Episodes.Title: Mr. Plow
Episodes.Description: Homer and Barney become competitors in the snow-plowing business.

Episodes.Title: Lisa's First Word
Episodes.Description: While trying to get Maggie to say her first word, Marge and Homer reminisce about Bart's and Lisa's first words.

Episodes.Title: Homer's Triple Bypass
Episodes.Description: Homer sees a discount doctor for a coronary bypass.

Episodes.Title: Marge vs. the Monorail
Episodes.Description: When Springfield gets a sudden windfall, a charismatic traveling salesman convinces the town to build a monorail.

Episodes.Title: Selma's Choice
Episodes.Description: After seeing Aunt Gladys die alone, Aunt Selma wants to get married and have a baby... until she spends a day babysitting Bart and Lisa at Duff Gardens.

Episodes.Title: Brother from the Same Planet
Episodes.Description: When Homer neglects Bart once too often, Bart goes to the Big Brother program to get a new father figure. Stung, Homer replaces Bart with a little brother.

Episodes.Title: I Love Lisa
Episodes.Description: Chief Wiggum's son has a crush on Lisa after she gives him a Valentine out of pity.

Episodes.Title: Duffless
Episodes.Description: After a DUI, Homer swears off beer for a month. Meanwhile, Bart and Lisa's sibling rivalry plays out in the school science fair.

Episodes.Title: Last Exit to Springfield
Episodes.Description: Union president Homer fights to keep the dental plan.

Episodes.Title: So It's Come to This: A Simpsons Clip Show
Episodes.Description: An April Fools' Day prank provides the jumping-off point for Simpson family flashbacks.

Episodes.Title: The Front
Episodes.Description: Lisa and Bart write an Itchy and Scratchy episode; Homer makes up a missing high-school credit.

Episodes.Title: Whacking Day
Episodes.Description: Lisa takes a stand against Springfield's annual snake-bashing festival.

Episodes.Title: Marge in Chains
Episodes.Description: Overwhelmed by her family's demands during a flu epidemic, Marge accidentally shoplifts at the Kwik-E-Mart and winds up in prison.

Episodes.Title: Krusty Gets Kancelled
Episodes.Description: Krusty's Hollywood pals help when his show is canceled after a new star causes his ratings to plummet.

Episodes.Title: Homer's Barbershop Quartet
Episodes.Description: Homer recalls when he, Apu, Barney and Principal Skinner became recording icons.

Episodes.Title: Cape Feare
Episodes.Description: The Simpsons go incognito to avoid the newly paroled Sideshow Bob, who's out to get Bart.

Episodes.Title: Homer Goes to College
Episodes.Description: Homer takes Nuclear Physics 101 at the local college, where he gets a trio of nerdy tutors expelled for extracurricular activities.

Episodes.Title: Rosebud
Episodes.Description: Burns longs for a childhood toy that winds up in the grip of Maggie.

Episodes.Title: Treehouse of Horror IV
Episodes.Description: Homer sells his soul; Vampire Burns invites the Simpsons for dinner; Bart sees a gremlin damaging his school bus.

Episodes.Title: Marge on the Lam
Episodes.Description: Marge's wild night out with neighbor Ruth includes running from the police in Ruth's car, stolen from her ex.

Episodes.Title: Bart's Inner Child
Episodes.Description: Springfield emulates Bart after he's praised by a self-help guru.

Episodes.Title: Boy-Scoutz 'N the Hood
Episodes.Description: After a reckless Squishee bender with Milhouse, Bart wakes to the shocking realization that he joined the Junior Campers. Lured by pocketknives and knot-tying lessons, Bart assimilates into the group but then must face the father-son rafting trip.

Episodes.Title: The Last Temptation of Homer
Episodes.Description: Homer struggles with his attraction to new coworker Mindy, a beautiful engineer whose love for doughnuts is equal to his own.

Episodes.Title: $pringfield (Or, How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love Legalized Gambling)
Episodes.Description: Legalized gambling comes to Springfield, and Marge becomes addicted; Robert Goulet entertains at Bart's casino for kids.

Episodes.Title: Homer the Vigilante
Episodes.Description: Homer leads a vigilante group to catch the Springfield Cat Burglar, who then robs the museum.

Episodes.Title: Bart Gets Famous
Episodes.Description: When an on-air remark catapults Bart to instant stardom, he finds that fame isn't all it's cracked up to be.

Episodes.Title: Homer and Apu
Episodes.Description: Homer accompanies Apu to the Kwik-E-Mart home office--in India--after Apu is fired.

Episodes.Title: Lisa vs. Malibu Stacy
Episodes.Description: Lisa's outrage over the gender stereotypes reinforced by a new talking doll prompts her to confront the dollmaker.

Episodes.Title: Deep Space Homer
Episodes.Description: Homer and Barney compete to be the first "average" American in space.

Episodes.Title: Homer Loves Flanders
Episodes.Description: Flanders' extra ticket to the big game makes him Homer's new best friend, a role that sorely tests Flanders' patience.

Episodes.Title: Bart Gets an Elephant
Episodes.Description: Bart wins an elephant, but Homer won't let him keep it.

Episodes.Title: Burns' Heir
Episodes.Description: Bart is picked to be Burns' heir and moves into the Burns mansion, prompting Homer and Marge to hire a deprogrammer to get him back.

Episodes.Title: Sweet Seymour Skinner's Baadasssss Song
Episodes.Description: Bart takes his dog to school, which gets Skinner fired, which in turn leaves Bart missing his archnemesis.

Episodes.Title: The Boy Who Knew Too Much
Episodes.Description: Bart can clear Mayor Quimby's nephew of a charge of battery, but only by implicating himself as a hooky player.

Episodes.Title: Lady Bouvier's Lover
Episodes.Description: Grandpa Simpson falls for Marge's mother, but loses out to a competitor; Bart gets ripped off shopping at home with Homer's credit card.

Episodes.Title: Secrets of a Successful Marriage
Episodes.Description: Homer teaches a class on marriage, but sharing secrets about his own union gets him kicked out of the house.

Episodes.Title: Bart of Darkness
Episodes.Description: Stuck in his room with a broken leg, Bart hears a high-pitched scream. When he looks through his telescope, he sees a guilty Ned Flanders burying the evidence.

Episodes.Title: Lisa's Rival
Episodes.Description: Lisa feels threatened when a new girl moves to Springfield: Allison is smart, pretty, a great saxophone player and a crack diorama builder. Lisa tries to befriend her new rival, but she's consumed with envy and competitiveness.

Episodes.Title: Another Simpsons Clip Show
Episodes.Description: After reading the weepy best-seller The Bridges of Madison County, Marge sits down with the family and recalls romantic moments, along with temptations from her bowling instructor Jacques and Homer's coworker Mindy.

Episodes.Title: Itchy & Scratchy Land
Episodes.Description: The family's trip to Itchy & Scratchy Land takes an unexpected turn when high-tech robots malfunction and become violent.

Episodes.Title: Sideshow Bob Roberts
Episodes.Description: Mayor Quimby pardons attempted murderer Sideshow Bob, who then runs against Quimby for mayor.

Episodes.Title: Treehouse of Horror V
Episodes.Description: Lack of beer and cable TV make Homer a crazed killer; the present is altered by a time-traveling Homer; and Principal Skinner turns detention students into food.

Episodes.Title: Bart's Girlfriend
Episodes.Description: Bart learns that the good Reverend Lovejoy's daughter is really bad.

Episodes.Title: Lisa on Ice
Episodes.Description: Lisa's surprising ability at hockey spawns jealousy in Bart and a showdown when their teams meet.

Episodes.Title: Homer Badman
Episodes.Description: When Homer gropes for a gummy candy stuck to the babysitter's pants, she mistakes his intentions and turns the town against him.

Episodes.Title: Grampa vs. Sexual Inadequacy
Episodes.Description: Grandpa's homemade tonic puts life back in the Simpson bedroom, so he and Homer hit the road to sell the stuff.

Episodes.Title: Fear of Flying
Episodes.Description: When they try to go on vacation, the family discovers Marge's debilitating fear of flying. Marge consults a psychoanalyst to find the source of her baffling fear.

Episodes.Title: Homer the Great
Episodes.Description: Homer joins the secret society of the Stonecutters and is suddenly exalted when the brethren discover his birthmark. The ancient order is shaken to the core by the ineptitude of its new Chosen One.

Episodes.Title: And Maggie Makes Three
Episodes.Description: The story of Maggie's birth is told in flashbacks: after Homer quits the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant to pursue his dream of working at a bowling alley, Marge reveals that she is pregnant.

Episodes.Title: Bart's Comet
Episodes.Description: When Bart is forced to assist Principal Skinner in early-morning astronomy observations, he discovers a giant comet heading towards Springfield. Facing impending doom, the entire town shows up at the Flanders family bomb shelter.

Episodes.Title: Homie the Clown
Episodes.Description: Krusty the Clown's reckless spending forces him to open a clown college to keep afloat. New graduate Homer discovers the perks and perils of being Krusty.

Episodes.Title: Bart vs. Australia
Episodes.Description: After tricking an Australian boy into accepting a collect call, Bart flies Down Under to apologize.

Episodes.Title: Homer vs. Patty and Selma
Episodes.Description: A loan from Patty and Selma makes Homer their slave; Bart is forced to take ballet.

Episodes.Title: A Star Is Burns
Episodes.Description: Film critic Jay Sherman is among the judges at the Springfield Film Festival, which Mr. Burns conspires to win by bribing some judges.

Episodes.Title: Lisa's Wedding
Episodes.Description: A fortuneteller predicts Lisa's engagement and wedding to a fellow student from an upper-crust British family.

Episodes.Title: Two Dozen and One Greyhounds
Episodes.Description: The Simpson household's overrun with puppies--the offspring of Santa's Little Helper and his new girlfriend from which Mr. Burns would love to make a greyhound-skin tuxedo.

Episodes.Title: The PTA Disbands
Episodes.Description: Bart helps precipitate a teachers strike, but he rues his handiwork when Marge takes over for Mrs. Krabappel.

Episodes.Title: Round Springfield
Episodes.Description: Bart winds up in the hospital as a result of eating Krusty cereal, and when Lisa comes to visit him, she is reunited with her sax idol.

Episodes.Title: The Springfield Connection
Episodes.Description: Marge joins the police force after thwarting a criminal, and Homer thinks he now has a free ride as a cop's spouse.

Episodes.Title: Lemon of Troy
Episodes.Description: Springfield boys try to recapture the town's beloved lemon tree after it's stolen.

Episodes.Title: Who Shot Mr. Burns? (1)
Episodes.Description: Mr. Burns makes many enemies when he steals the oil discovered beneath Springfield Elementary.

Episodes.Title: Who Shot Mr. Burns? (2)
